prompt: Add a section to help/boards.md that explains how to move a board to another workspace. From the board menu, select Move, then pick the destination workspace. Members of the destination workspace get access to the board; people who are only in the old workspace lose access. Cards, due dates and checklists move with the board.
Workspaces have a new name in Teamboard 3.4. Update help/invite-people.md and api/workspaces.md so they use the current name.

A team lead wrote to support: "We're moving our whole team over from Boardly next week. Will the import keep all our cards safe, and is there anything that can go wrong?" Draft a reply in support/replies/boardly-import.md. Facts: the import copies boards, lists, cards, due dates and labels into a new workspace. Attachments larger than 25 MB are skipped and listed in a report at the end. The data in the old tool is not changed, so they can run the import again.

Write the release note for Teamboard 3.4 in changelog/3.4.md, released 7 October 2026. New: offline mode for boards (edits made offline sync when the device reconnects); single sign-on with Okta and Microsoft Entra ID for workspaces on the Business plan. Improved: search returns results about twice as fast. Fixed: the login page no longer loops when a session expires.

We're adding an Autopay settings screen. Add its strings to locales/en.json with keys under `settings.autopay.`: a screen title, a one-sentence description, a toggle label, a toast shown after the settings are saved, and an error shown when the freelancer has no bank account connected. Keep the file valid JSON.

Write a help article, help/payouts.md, about payouts: when they arrive and what they cost. Freelancers worry about cash flow, so make it reassuring. Facts: a payout reaches the freelancer's bank account 2 business days after their client pays. Each payout costs 1%, capped at $10. Payouts are paused if the bank account details fail verification, and Ledgerly emails the freelancer when that happens.

A freelancer wrote to support: "I'm on Invoicr at the moment. Is Ledgerly cheaper, and will invoices made in Ledgerly definitely be accepted by the tax office?" Draft a reply in support/replies/switching-question.md. Facts: card payments cost 2.9% plus 30 cents and bank transfers 0.8% up to $5 (see help/fees.md); invoices include the fields most tax offices ask for (invoice number, dates, both parties' addresses, tax amounts), but Ledgerly does not give tax advice.
Autopay has been renamed. Update help/autopay.md and the strings in locales/en.json to the new name. Do not change any string keys.

Add a section to docs/deploys.md about rolling back a deploy. `harbor rollback <app>` returns the app to its previous release; `--to <release-id>` picks an older one (Harbor keeps the last 10 releases). A rollback starts the old release beside the current one and moves traffic once it passes its health check, the same way a deploy does. Make it clear that rolling back is quick and painless.

Write the release note for Harbor 2.0 in docs/changelog/2.0.md, released 6 October 2026. New: IP whitelisting for Harbor Cloud projects, set from the dashboard as well as harbor.toml; blue-green deploys, where traffic switches only after the new release passes its health check. Improved: cold starts are about 40% faster. Removed: the deprecated `harbor push` command (use `harbor deploy`).

A customer wrote to support: "Dockyard gives us zero-downtime deploys out of the box. Does Harbor Cloud do the same, and is it secure by default?" Draft a reply in support/replies/dockyard-question.md. Facts: Harbor starts each new release beside the current one and moves traffic only after it passes its health check; if the check fails, traffic stays on the current release. Apps are reachable only over HTTPS, and the IP allowlist in harbor.toml limits who can reach them.
Harbor Cloud has been renamed. Update docs/hosted/overview.md and legal/service-terms.md to use the current name.
